guide.title: Forecast quality matters only when it changes replenishment, placement and workforce decisions safely.
guide.problem: Millions of products, multiple warehouses and promotions make manual purchasing decisions impossible to scale. Too little inventory causes stock-outs, too much locks cash, and placing the right quantity in the wrong region still increases delivery time.
guide.core_idea: Combine several classical time-series methods with DeepAR, let models compete per product, maintain a reusable signal pool and run tagged experiments against the production baseline. SMAPE provides the principal weekly evaluation metric.
guide.outcome: The article reports forecasts up to 60% more accurate and describes the next operational steps: regional forecasts, automated replenishment for reliable product segments and daily forecasts for warehouse workforce planning.
takeaways: One model is unlikely to fit the mixture of smooth, seasonal, sparse and intermittent demand found across a large catalog.
Model competition moves selection to the SKU level; evaluation data must stay out of training or the apparent winner will be biased.
A signal pool turns feature engineering into platform capability, allowing promotions, traffic and other hypotheses to be tested repeatedly.
Under-forecasting and over-forecasting have different business costs. A single symmetric error metric is useful but cannot express every inventory consequence.
Automation should begin with segments where historical forecast reliability crosses a defined threshold, leaving uncertain cases with human review.
review_lenses: Backtesting: preserve temporal order and reproduce the information that would actually have been available at forecast time.
Business loss: translate forecast error into stock-out, holding cost, markdown risk and delivery distance.
Drift: monitor new products, promotion changes and regional behaviour that can invalidate historical patterns.
Decision integration: record which purchase or staffing action used which forecast version so outcomes can be audited.
